utterances.text: I think it's me. Yes, it's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And person immediately to your right hand with the moustache, who's that?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Balaban.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The man next to him in the tie?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Smajil Zahirovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the men next to him, on the far left?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ibro Paunovic. Or Ibrahim, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All four of you worked at RZR Ljubija before the war; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You and Mr. Balaban were Serbs, while Mr. Paunovic and Mr. Zahirovic were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. At the time, I was a Yugoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Paunovic and Mr. Zahirovic, Muslims?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I know about Zahirovic for sure, that he's a Muslim and as for Paunovic. We were good friends. I believe that he is a Goranac by origin. A Gorani man.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What was his religious background?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know which religion the Gorani people are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Paunovic and Mr. Zahirovic, have you ever seen either of them after the war?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Except for Balaban.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that some of your people were in Omarska. The Chamber has received evidence that Mr. Paunovic disappeared from Omarska in June 1992, P2303 and P5588. Was he one of the people you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? This photograph is distracting me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the last -- if you have someone on your mind, in what context. Needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you mentioned earlier in your testimony, or in the recorded portion of your interview that we played for you, that some of your people were in Omarska. Was Mr. Paunovic who evidence indicates disappeared from Omarska in June 1992 and who you've never seen again, one of the people that you were thinking of, was one of your people that was in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Because Smajil Zahirovic was living at my place and I know from that that he gone to Omarska. That's why I said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31041 receives exhibit number P7626, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, earlier today in the context of resources, company resources, mobilised by the Prijedor SJB, you mentioned Koricanske Stijene. What RZR Ljubija resources were used for at Koricanske Stijene was to dispose of the bodies of more than 100 Muslim men who had been murdered by members of the Prijedor police; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the number, but from the trials of some individuals over Koricanske Stijene, I know they were members of the public security centre. And about the machinery, I had explained that it was requisitioned by the public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, again, you've answered parts of the question but not all of it. What that machinery was used for was to dispose of the bodies of the people who'd been murdered; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31036.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You've seen this before. This is a certificate for a pistol given to you by Simo Drljaca in appreciation for the co-operation and assistance you provided to the Prijedor police. You received this pistol; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. But, please, in my statement, in fact, in my evidence in the Stakic case, I gave a more detailed explanation how that pistol was gifted to me. If necessary, I can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you can keep it to a sentence or two, I'd invite you to do so now.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can do that even more briefly. That pistol was given to me by the minister of economy of Serbia. He sent it through Mr. Lovro, the head of the public security centre. At that time, I was at loggerheads with Simo Drljaca, and this man had come from Novi Sad, told me that he had brought me this pistol. I said I did not have a licence, and he signed this document so that I can get a licence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this isn't a licence. It's a statement referring to co-operation and assistance; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, this is an explanation that would allow me to get a licence. He could have written it differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you're right, and, at the same time you're, to some extent, misleading the witness because it clearly in the last line says that this document serves to get a registration for the weapon and that's what the witness is referring to. And now to say it's not a licence, strictly spoken, it is true, but at the same time, it's confusing the witness and I invite you to refrain from doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take the point can we have 65 ter 33431.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, I see that the pistol was given to the witness by a certain Mr. Lovro, as recorded, but this document seems to purport to come from the Ministry of the Interior, Security Services, Banja Luka public security station. And it doesn't mention Mr. Lovro as the giver of this present. On the contrary, it is given in gratitude for the witness's co-operation that he provided to the -- public security station. According to the document. So my question to you then is: How does Lovro, Mr. Lovro come into this? It looks like it's a gift from the public security station.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. I told you the whole path this pistol followed before it came to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one small question. You said he signed the document. Do I have to understand that this document is not signed by Simo Drljaca or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I read to you this Mr. Lovro told you that he had brought you this pistol. You said you didn't have a licence. And: "He signed this document so that I can get a licence." But that is -- you are then referring not to Mr. Lovro any further but to Mr. Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No -- no, you are right. It is correct because this is a document from the public security centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33431.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a certificate also stating, "Grateful for co-operation and assistance provided." Also coming from Mr. Drljaca. And this time the pistol's going to a man named Milorad Sipka. He was the director of the Eastern Mine, also known as the Tomasica mine in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the last two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 31036 receives exhibit number P7627. 65 ter number 33431 receives exhibit number P7628.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7627 and P7628 are admitted into evidence. Could you tell us, witness, had that same Mr. Lovro come to that other person to give him a pistol? Or don't you know or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. At the time when I was at the public security centre, Mr. Sipka was not there. I was not present at that transaction. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, just before leaving Mr. Drljaca, you know that in 1993 he was promoted to a position in the minister of the interior's cabinet; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33383, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be another portion of your Stakic testimony. You were asked: "When you say that Simo Drljaca left and took up a position as a deputy, did he go to Bijeljina at that time? You answer: "I think he was supposed to be based in Bijeljina, his office should have been in Bijeljina. I have information that he spent quite some time in Novi Sad. What was the reason for his stay in Novi Sad, I really don't know. But he would turn up in Prijedor, too, and quite often." You were asked: "Was that a promotion or a demotion for Simo Drljaca?" And you responded: "If a person is first the chief of the MUP of Prijedor, and then leaves to take up the position of a deputy or an assistant - I'm not sure what the official title of the position was - well, that should be considered a promotion." Do you stand by this portion of your Stakic testimony as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I must confess that this testimony was a long time ago, and I'm not sure whether he was a deputy or maybe a deputy of a representative, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to focus on the part I'm most interested in, does this portion of your testimony refresh your recollection that he was promoted in 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll include that in the portions for which an exhibit number has already been reserved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Only this page or also -- because I see that on the previous page of what is in e-court now, that's page 4 out of 96 pages. That there's more said about the position Simo Drljaca took up. That's immediately preceding the portion you read to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course, we're happy to include anything the Chamber considers relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but just to better understand page 11758, I think the introduction at page 11757, where it's described, "He was to be the first man of Republika Srpska MUP with headquarters at Bijeljina." That perhaps sheds some additional light on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Having heard the portion that Judge Orie has reminded you of, of your Stakic testimony, does that, again, refresh your recollection as to what position he was to get in 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for giving me this opportunity. After he was in Bijeljina, he stayed in Novi Sad, and after all these events, he returned to his position as the head of the public security centre in Prijedor, if that is of any assistance. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue was whether Drljaca, to become the first man of the Republika Srpska MUP, with headquarters at Bijeljina, whether that refreshes your memory as to what kind of a position Mr. Drljaca was appointed to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have 65 ter 32871.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a piece in Kozarski Vjesnik published the 6th of November, 1992. At the top, under the reference to Mr. Karadzic, we read that -- we read the description that Kozarski Vjesnik is taking advantage of the presence of numerous top civilian and military leaders of Republika Srpska. Now you know, don't you, that the Republika Srpska Assembly was held in Prijedor at the end of October and very beginning of November 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And turning to page 2 in the English and on the left in the B/C/S of page 1, it's the bottom here of page 2 in the English and the start of the article reflecting General Mladic's quotes in the B/C/S. We see General Mladic is quoted. Now you testified on direct that Mladic was never in Prijedor. Does this refresh your recollection that he was there in the fall of 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know that he has been in Prijedor. I repeated that umpteen times.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And anyone who was in Prijedor at the end of October 1992 would have been able to see with their own eyes the devastation that had been wreaked on Muslim neighbourhoods, Muslim villages in the vicinity of the town; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 32871.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 32871 receives exhibit number P7629.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7629 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P3278.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Give the P number again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 3278, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll be looking for page 19 in the English; 17 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a transcript of some interviews with Prijedor Chronicle, including one with you. At the end of your remarks in the middle of the page in both languages, you say: "I estimate that there is a high level of understanding between us and the military, and especially good" -- sorry. "Exceptionally good co-operation with the local leadership of Prijedor municipality. I do not think that Ljubija deserves to be especially highlighted because it fits into the mosaic of joint efforts to create this new" - and there's a suggested translation of "system, which is our goal." Now do you stand behind what I've read back to you from this interview about the high level of understanding between RZR Ljubija and the military and the exceptional co-operation with the local leadership of Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you personally knew the 43rd Brigade commander, Vladimir Arsic; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You attended meetings he organised; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33381, page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, beginning here at line 10 you were asked: "Did you know Mr. Arsic? I'm not mentioning his ranks because -- his rank because the rank changed." You answer: "Yes, I knew him." You explain his positions in 1990 and 1991. And you say: "And if you will allow me, having said that, I knew him. I had opportunity to attend meetings organised by him in my capacity as a businessman. I believe that he is a native of Serbia. He was from Serbia. He was exceptionally -- I would like to use a word 'arrogant' but that is not what would describe him. He was domineering. When he issued orders, he did it in a very domineering tone." And you add a few lines later: "He just issued orders and he expected people to obey his orders and to deliver." Do you stand by the portions of your Stakic testimony that I've just read back to you?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were then asked when we are talking about him we also mentioned the sentence which he used to explain to other non-military how things would develop from then on, and you relied: "The sentence was things that he said, they would be. That's why I said previously that he didn't put up with discussions. I mean, yes, the discussion was okay, but eventually, he had the last call, and things would be what he decided them to be." Do you also stand by that portion of your Stakic testimony?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I do, but I want to add one thing: Typical soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now aside from him, you also met with a lieutenant-colonel named Radovan Rajlic in the 43rd Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, one of the things that needs further explanation. When first asked whether you attended meetings he organised, you said no. And then a portion was read of your Stakic testimony in which you said you attended meetings he had organised. You attended them as a businessman. Which of the two -- why -- why you first say I did not attend; and in Stakic you said you did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not attend meetings that he had militarily with his associates but I attended meetings in restaurants that he had organised there, where we discussed the economy, the military, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you carefully listen, then, to the question before you answer it. Because Mr. Traldi did not ask you whether you attended any military meetings but whether you attended any meetings he had organised. And apparently it was mixed military and business meetings, as you explained later on. So, therefore, carefully listen to the questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you've previously testified that RZR Ljubija handed over all its mining explosives to the army before the war. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, but I don't know if the term is -- well, it was in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you also, at Colonel Arsic's request, gave the army geodesic maps of the RZR Ljubija property; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: That was in 1991. These are geodesic maps because we had a service that handled that. We had enough maps for the area of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And those would show which areas of the mines were working and which areas were not; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to step away from the 43rd Brigade for a second. Can we have 65 ter 01369. Now this is a list of territorial maintenance resources approved by General Mladic for Operation Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in the English and zoom in on the left in the B/C/S, point 10, in both languages, we see Ljubija RZ or RZ Ljubija in the original. Did the Ljubija RZR serve as a resource for the 14th Logistics Base for the VRS throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: We provided services to the army. You can draw your own conclusion. We maintained some of their machinery and they paid us regularly for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you two very specific questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but could we first receive an answer to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was just going to break it up into two specific questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I leave it in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, providing services to the army including serving as a resource for the VRS's 14th Logistics Base like we see in this document; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And second, did RZR Ljubija serve as a resource for the 14th Logistics Base throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know of this term, logistics base. I don't know what is meant by that. We did provide services to the military, that is to say maintaining their equipment, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 01369 receives exhibit number P7630.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. The equipment which is listed here, that was not equipment that was provided by the mine, by the Ljubija mine, or did that also include any equipment that had been -- had been ordered to give to the military by the mine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know of this document. I've explained before that on the basis of mobilisation, we did give some of this machinery to the military and also in Prijedor, we maintained some of their machines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And maintenance of your own machinery which was mobilised by the military, where did that maintenance take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the central work-shop in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because you earlier testified that once you had to -- you were demanded to give equipment, that they would take it, take it elsewhere, and then upon return, it was yours again. Now I do understand that some of your equipment but also some of the original army equipment was kept in your premises for maintenance, though still --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- though still under control of the military.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that your previous answer is not -- is not accurate? Could you please answer my question whether, then, you withdraw your previous answer as inaccurate or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, mobilisation of the mechanization of the Ljubija mines occurred from 1992 onwards. Certain machines that were not ours but were military machines were maintained at the central work-shop in Prijedor. As for the return of our machines, they were maintained in our central work-shop in Prijedor. Nobody else had authority over those machines while they were being maintained by us. There were certain bills that were sent for the services rendered, for the maintenance of the machinery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But your own machines which were mobilised - so machines that did not originally come from the army but was your equipment, your machinery - which were then -- I think you said requisitions - I must say I ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Requisitioned, then it could be that being requisitioned or being mobilised for army purposes that it would still be in your garages for maintenance while still under control of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assert that the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it was requisitioned or mobilised for army purposes where then was that equipment maintained and serviced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mobilisation sometimes took a month or two or somewhat longer. When the machinery was returned, we would maintain it in our work-shop and then it would stay there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to go back to one of your answers a moment ago regarding geodesic maps. Now, in your interview you stated that you'd -- that Colonel Arsic had requested those from you at the beginning of 1992. In your testimony a moment ago, you said 1991. Do you grant now that it may have been the beginning of 1992 when the request was made?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's possible that it's the end of 1991, beginning of 1992. It's more than 20 years that all of this happened. Don't expect me at my age after all these years to be able to say exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P7385.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's a P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an annual report of RZR Ljubija dated December 1992. You ordered this report to be made; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 3 in both languages, in the middle, we read -- and in the English -- sorry, it's the bottom in the B/C/S. "Additional measures were taken to ensure general security in the enterprise and very close co-operation was also continued with the army Main Staff and the public security centre."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where are you reading from?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In the English, it's the paragraph just below the capitalised words, "AUTHORITIES, POLICE and the ARMY," and it's the second half of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: If thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the B/C/S the very end of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you see that text, sir?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, your co-operation with the army was primarily with the 14th Logistics Base and the 43rd Brigade, as we've seen; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. The 14th Logistics Brigade? This is the first I hear of it. I don't know what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it also says immediately before that that, already in early June, only around ten days after the fighting in the town, the army and police took over all direct securing of facilities, property and persons." Now during your examination-in-chief, you suggested that your security guards just happened to be wearing military uniforms. What your report at the time says is the truth, that it was the army doing the securing; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I think that this is wrong. I would again like to ask the Prosecutor where it says that, that it was the army that had secured that. That is a misrepresentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I read the English literally. I understand the relevant B/C/S words - just apologising for my limited skills in the language - to appear at the end of the third line in the paragraph where it says [B/C/S spoken], which I understand to be the part translated as "army and police."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it -- do you -- is -- you still take it that it's misrepresented? Then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, Your Honour. With your permission I would like to read out the entire sentence to the witness. It is the first sentence in the last paragraph in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's another part. That was not the part quoted. You can read it to the witness if it is of any relevance in re-examination. And, of course, Mr. Traldi is certainly aware that if by leaving out another portion he would distort the gist of the text he is now warned because he is aware that he shouldn't do that. We'll wait for you to see -- we'll first wait for Mr. Traldi to see whether he repeats his question, as he did, and then, second, we'll hear from you in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think we are referring to the same sentence. And so the simplest thing is to address it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Witness, if you see where the words [B/C/S spoken] appear at the beginning of the last paragraph in B/C/S, if you could just read aloud from there to the words [B/C/S spoken]?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that there is a problem with the translation again from B/C/S into English and I think that the meaning of the sentence has been completely distorted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing you should then say, Mr. Stojanovic, is there is a translation issue here. Leave it to that. Don't tell whether it changes the gist of what is written or not. Mr. Traldi asked the witness to read the original B/C/S version. So, therefore, if you would have waited, then we'll see what comes out in the English language. Please proceed. The witness is invited to read what Mr. Traldi invited him to read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Already in the beginning of the month of June, that is to say, only some ten days from when the fighting took place in town, complete direct security of buildings, property and persons were taken over by the military and police. Additional measures were also taken in carrying out general security in the company but what also continued was the very close co-operation with the Main Staff of the army and the centre of public security."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll put a form of the question that I would have put to you initially. We haven't read in there anything about people who happened to be wearing military uniforms. What we've read about is the army, the military, the police; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you allow me, at the time in Prijedor there was at least 15 to 18 armies. Every village had its own army and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what I asked you about is your report describing your security that you also testified about, I put it to you, inconsistently during your direct examination. What we see here is the army, the military, the police, not people who happened to be in uniform; right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: You're not allowing me to explain the situation. You mention --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're invited to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question. It's about -- I can imagine that it's about inconsistency between what we read here and what you testified before. But, Mr. Traldi, please put it again to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read here in your report describing your company's security that you also testified about, I put it to you inconsistently, during your direct examination, what we see here is the army, the military, and also the police doing the security. There is no reference to people who happened to be wearing military uniforms. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you point me to the reference to people who happened to be wearing military uniforms in this report?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the vice-president of the municipality, the man called Cigo and he had his own army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, we cannot yell at witnesses. I heard this [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lukic, only in exceptional circumstances, counsel who is not examining the witness should intervene. The -- if there's any rule that there should be no yelling, and I do agree that there should not be, that is valid for you as well. Because you were yelling at least as much as -- let me say, you used the volume of your voice which was at least similar to, if not even higher, than Mr. Traldi did. Mr. Traldi, could you repeat the question. And, Witness, could I invite you to answer the question rather than tell us things that were not asked.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: With regard to the sight translation of the sentence that was provided, the sentence is ambiguous in the original. It can either be by or from the military and the police. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't think that will change my question but if anyone disagrees, I'd invite them to say so now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, there's nothing in your report about your security, produced by your company, at your direction, referring to people who happened to be wearing uniforms. It refers to the army, it refers to the military, and it also referred to the police. That's the truth; right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 7 in both languages. Sorry, can we have 8 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see here a list of weapons and equipment provided to, on the right side, different war units. We see the code 4777 for all of the weapons and equipment. That's the code for the 43rd Brigade of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to the next page in B/C/S, we see motor vehicles, machines and equipment provided to different units. We see a lot of 4777 again. And some 8316, that's the quote for the 5th Kozara Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at the top we see 6817 and 5456, those are VRS brigades, not based in Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do we have the same page in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the list of motor vehicles, machines and equipment starts at the bottom of the page in English and continues to the next. But the specific numbers I was drawing the witness's attention to, all appear on this portion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall what unit 6817 applies to?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you'd agree with those numbers there that the RZR Ljubija was providing motor vehicles, machines and equipment to VRS units both within Prijedor and units from outside it; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: The 43rd Brigade was constantly outside of Prijedor from 1992 onwards. The 5th Kozara Brigade from 1992 onwards was also outside Prijedor. A very small part of machinery we provided to the air force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I see we're close to the time for the break. Your Honour, I am about to turn to a new topic and so if this is a good point -- otherwise I do have one other document I could use quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it would be better to take the break now. Could you -- First of all, Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you give us an impression as to how much time you would still need.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think approximately half an hour, Your Honour, but I can be more specific after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes to 2.00, because we take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To come back to the Chamber, I think half an hour may have been slightly ambitious. I will be within my original estimate so certainly less than a full hour but it may be a few minutes more than 30. In the interests of being as expeditious as possible, if we could have 65 ter 32870 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking aloud.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, here on our screens, sir, at the top of the page in the B/C/S we see an article titled, "Headed For Victory and Unity." Refers in the first paragraph to a meeting held in the great hall of the Ljubija RZR and it's dated 31 July, 1992, the article. At the bottom of the page in the English and the third paragraph in the B/C/S we see remarks by Colonel Arsic, discussing the decisive battle that is being fought for the Krajina. Now, this is one of the meetings that you attended with him and with other business and political figures; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As head of RZR Ljubija, you wouldn't have attended a meeting between civilian and military authorities and business people held in the great hall of RZR Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I certainly did not attend because I would remember that meeting. I have no memory of such a meeting. I must have been away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Were you in Prijedor at the end of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you lived in down-town Prijedor. The Chamber has received evidence that about a week before this meeting, more than 100 detainees at Keraterm camp were killed in room 3. You're aware of that crime; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the people you heard had been killed in Biscani, that also happened about a week, ten days before this meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, some -- from 11 July or 12th until the 20th, I was in Serbia. When the corridor was opened up, I took my son to Belgrade. It could have been in that interval, when I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I hadn't asked about your travel at the time. What I'd asked about was the people that you heard had been killed in Biscani, you'd heard that they were killed at ten days before this meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about the killing in Biscani, but I cannot locate it in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31866.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a press article not yet translated from a website called Balkan Transitional Justice, and we read, "Bosnia charges 15 Serbs for Zecovi massacre." And we see about five paragraphs down that the defendants are specifically charged with killing 29 men and women in Zecovi on July 25th, 1992. Did you also hear that Bosnian Muslims and Croats had been murdered in Zecovi shortly before the 31st of July?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time I did not know. But I know now after these people were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 65 ter 32870 and ask that 65 ter 31866 be marked for identification pending a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 32870 receives Exhibit P7631. 65 ter number 31866 receives Exhibit P7632.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7631 is admitted into evidence. P7632 is marked for identification. Mr. Traldi, I'm just looking at the 12 December, 12014. The way of introducing, pending prosecutions is uncommonly done by the Prosecution through websites, rather we have -- now, the witness does not contest that he heard about it, but I would certainly not encourage the Prosecution to provide us with this kind of typically legal information through websites where I've got no idea what weight to give to it. But there was no objection. It's just, perhaps, some guidance that there are better sources to present this evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33385, page 97.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a portion of your OTP interview. You say in the middle of the page: "From Prijedor non-Serbs, so I will use this terminology so I avoid saying Croats and Muslims, from Prijedor non-Serbs were sent to the territory of Federation. "In the beginning, they paid to avoid going, to avoid leaving or going to Federation ... and later they paid to go." First, do you stand behind the truthfulness and accuracy of the portion of your OTP interview I've just read back to you?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, the reason they were so desperate as to pay to leave was the crimes that some of which we've gone through today, the killings in Biscani and Zecovi that you've heard about, the crimes at Omarska, the crimes elsewhere in Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: You've explained it all to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, although are you trying to speed up, you should slow down when you are reading in order to get a good transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take the point, Your Honour. And I'd referred in line 14 to Zecovi and Omarska which weren't captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn now to graves on the RZR Ljubija property. You know that there were mass graves at Redak on the central mine property on Jakarina Kosa and on Tomasica on the eastern mine property; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: The name is not Radak; it's Redak. I've already explained that I saw it in 2003 in a map that was shown to me when these places were identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you know people - at least some of the people exhumed from Redak - were killed on central mine property in late July 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know the details, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have back -- and it's the version of 65 ter 32665 marked by the witness. I'm afraid my notes are incomplete. D1347. If we can zoom in on the middle of the aerial image.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to the left of the lake that we now see on the right, you know there's a mass grave in that area; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you help me, I don't know this light spot to the left of the lake, I suppose that is the deposit of waste from Ferox, judging by the shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And there's a -- there's a dumping-ground over there; right? Used by the RZR.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ferox is an independent enterprise but it's in the immediate vicinity of the mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the geodesic maps you provided the VRS would have identified this as an area where there was no mining going on; right? The geodesic maps provided to what was at the time the 343rd Brigade of the JNA that was transformed a couple of months later into the 43rd brigade of the VRS, under the same commander and the same deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: The maps were given in 1991, and according to the law, geodetical surveys are made every year to record any changes, and these maps were made to reflect the activity and works.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that bulldozers and excavators were being used by the VRS at this site between 20th and 25th of July, 1992. Now, when your company's records showed bulldozers working for the VRS at dumping sites where no mining was going on, nowhere near any front line, what did you think they were doing?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't think anything. It's the grounds of Ferox. They have their own machinery. At that time, I didn't have any information about activity in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You acknowledge, though, it's possible the VRS could have been involved in the burials at Tomasica; right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could we in one way or another clarify the issue of, in your questioning, referring to company records showing bulldozers working for the VRS, whereas the witness said Ferox had their own machinery. That's ... either by going to the records or by asking further questions to the witness, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Madam Registrar, could you assign a number to the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7633, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Mr. Traldi, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was just reminded of the same thing. I will have a few minutes tomorrow morning, probably about ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What about 65 ter 33385?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd called up the version marked by the witness. I had just done so somewhat awkwardly but the marked version is already in D1347.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, that's a different one and I've been corrected. 33385 is the interview and the interview, the number has been reserved for excerpts but I wouldn't be seeking to tender the whole thing and so I uploaded the excerpts that we seek to tender at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's both true for the interview and for the evidence given in the Stakic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, before we adjourn for the day, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in any way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony given today or whether that's testimony still to be given tomorrow. And I'm quite confident that tomorrow we'll not take that much of your time any further. We -- you may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 10th of November, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 10th day of November, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25
